91. Software Doesn't Really Exist

作者：Chad LaVigne

Software engineering is often compared to well-established disciplines such as civil engineering. There’s a problem with these analogies; unlike the very tangible products created by these traditional practices, software doesn’t really exist. Not in the traditional sense anyway. Those of us in the world of ones and zeros aren’t constrained by the same physical rules that bind classic engineering paradigms. While applying engineering principles to the software design phase works well, assuming you can implement the design in the same manner used by more traditional engineering approaches is unrealistic.

软件工程经常被比作土木工程这样成熟学科。这些类比有个问题；不像这些传统实践创造的非常有形的产品，软件其实并不存在。至少不是传统意义上。我们这些在一和零世界里的人不受束缚经典工程范式的同样物理规则约束。虽然把工程原则应用到软件设计阶段效果好，但假设你能以更传统工程方法用的同样方式实现设计是不现实的。

Both business and software are living, moving entities. Business requirements change rapidly due to things like newly acquired business partners and marketing strategies. This makes it very difficult to approach a software project in the same manner as a traditional engineering pursuit such as bridge construction. It is highly unlikely that you’ll be asked to move the location of a bridge halfway through a construction project. However, it is very likely that the acquisition of a business partner will require you to add support for organization-based content management to an application. This comparison should put things into perspective. We often say that software architecture decisions are difficult to change but not nearly so much as things that are literally and figuratively set in stone.

业务和软件都是活的、动的实体。业务需求因为新业务伙伴、营销策略等快速变化。这让以传统工程追求（如建桥）同样方式处理软件项目非常难。你被要求在建设项目中途移动桥位置的可能性极低。然而，获得业务伙伴很可能要求你给应用加基于组织的内容管理支持。这个比较应该把事情放到正确视角。我们经常说软件架构决定难改，但远不如字面和比喻上都刻在石头里的东西。

Knowing the products we build are pliable and that the requirements surrounding them are likely to change puts us in a different position than someone building an immovable object. Engineering endeavors of the physical flavor are much easier to implement in a “plan the work, work the plan” nature. With software, things need to be tackled in more of a “plan the work, massage the plan” fashion.

知道我们建的产品是可塑的、周围需求可能变，把我们放到和建不可动物不同的位置。物理口味的工程努力以「计划工作、执行计划」的本质容易实现。用软件，事情需要以更多「计划工作、按摩计划」的方式处理。

These differences aren’t always bad news—at times they can be advantageous. For example, you’re not necessarily constrained to building the components of a software system in a specific order so you can tackle high-risk issues first. This is in direct contrast to something like bridge construction, where there are many physical limitations surrounding the order in which tasks are accomplished.

这些差异不总是坏消息——有时它们有利。比如，你不一定被约束按特定顺序建软件系统组件，所以你可以先处理高风险问题。这和建桥这种事情直接对比，那里任务完成顺序有很多物理限制。

However, the flexibility of software engineering does present some issues, many of which are self-imposed. As architects, we are very aware of the “soft” nature of our craft and we like to solve problems. Worse yet, the business owners are vaguely aware of these facts. This makes it easy for them to push big changes. Don’t be too eager to accommodate large architectural changes just because it appeals to your solution-providing nature. Decisions like that can break an otherwise healthy project.

然而，软件工程的灵活性确实带来一些问题，很多是自找的。作为架构师，我们非常清楚自己手艺的「软」本质，我们喜欢解决问题。更糟，业务所有者隐约知道这些事实。这让他们容易推大变更。不要太急于容纳大架构变更，只因为它吸引你提供方案的本性。那种决定会破坏一个本来健康的项目。

Remember that a requirements document is not a blueprint, and software doesn’t really exist. The virtual objects that we create are easier to change than their physical-world counterparts, which is a good thing because many times they’re required to. It’s OK to plan as though we’re building an immovable object; we just can’t be surprised or unprepared when we’re asked to move said object.

记住需求文档不是蓝图，软件其实并不存在。我们创建的虚拟对象比物理世界对应物容易改，这是好事因为很多时候它们被要求改。像建不可动物一样计划没问题；我们只是不能在被要求移动该物时惊讶或没准备。

92. Learn a New Language

作者：Burkhardt Hufnagel

To be successful as an architect, you must be able to make yourself understood by people who don’t speak your native tongue. No, I’m not suggesting you learn Esperanto or even Klingon, but you should at least speak basic Business, and Testing. And, if you aren’t fluent in Programmer, you should make that a top priority.

要做成功的架构师，你必须能让不说你母语的人理解你。不，我不是建议你学世界语甚至克林贡语，但你至少该说基本的业务语和测试语。而且，如果你不流利说程序员语，你应该把它当第一优先。

If you don’t see the value in learning other languages, consider the following scenario. The business people want a change made to an existing system, so they call a meeting with the architect and programmers to discuss it. Unfortunately, none of the technical team speaks Business and none of the business people speaks Programmer. The meeting will likely go something like this:

如果你没看到学其他语言的价值，想想以下场景。业务人想对现有系统做变更，所以他们和架构师、程序员开会讨论。不幸的是，技术团队没人说业务语，业务人没人说程序员语。会议可能这样进行：

A business person talks for a minute about the need for a relatively simple • enhancement to an existing product, and explains how making the change will enable the sales team to increase both market and mind share.

一个业务人说一分钟需要对现有产品做相对简单增强，解释做这个变怎么让销售团队增加市场份额和心智份额。

While the business person is still speaking, the architect starts sketching • some kind of occult symbols on a notepad and enters into quiet argument with the one of the programmers in their strange multisyllabic tongue.

业务人还在说时，架构师开始在便签上画某种神秘符号，用他们奇怪的多音节语言和一个程序员小声争论。

Eventually the business person finishes and looks expectantly at the • architect.

最后业务人说完，期待地看着架构师。

After the whispered argument completes, the architect walks to the white- • board and begins drawing several complex diagrams that are supposed to represent multiple views of the existing system while explaining (in complex technical terms) why the requested enhancement is virtually impossible without major changes and may actually require a complete redesign/rewrite of the entire system.

小声争论结束后，架构师走到白板开始画几个复杂图——应该表示现有系统多视图——同时（用复杂技术术语）解释为什么请求的增强不大改实际上不可能、可能需要整个系统完全重设计/重写。

The business people (who understood little of the diagram and less of the • explanation) are openly stunned and find it hard to believe that something so simple would require such massive changes. They begin to wonder if the architect is serious or just making things up to avoid making the change.

业务人（几乎没看懂图、更少听懂解释）公开震惊，难信这么简单的事需要这么大变更。他们开始怀疑架构师是认真还是在编造来避免做变更。

Meanwhile, the architect and programmers are just as surprised that the • business people don’t see how the “minor” change will require major modifications to the core system functionality.

同时，架构师和程序员同样惊讶业务人看不到「小」变更怎么需要核心系统功能大改。

And therein lies the problem. Neither group understands how the other thinks or what half of the words they use means. This leads to mistrust and miscommunication. It’s a basic psychological principle that people are more comfortable with those who are similar to them than those who are different from them.

问题就在那。两组都不理解对方怎么想、用的词一半什么意思。这导致不信任和误传。基本心理学原则是：人们对和自己相似的人比对不同的人更舒服。

Imagine how the aforementioned scenario might change if the architect were able to explain the issues to the business folk in terms they understand and relay the business issues to the programmers in terms they understand. Instead of surprise and mistrust, the result would be agreement and approval.

想象一下如果架构师能用业务人懂的术语解释问题、用程序员懂的术语转达业务问题，前述场景会怎么变。结果不是惊讶和不信任，而是同意和批准。

I’m not saying that learning multiple languages will cure all your problems, but it will help prevent the miscommunications and misunderstandings that lead to problems.

我不是说学多种语言会治好你所有问题，但它会帮你防止导致问题的误传和误解。

For those of you who decide this makes sense, I wish you success on your journey. Or, as the Klingons say, Qapla !

对觉得这有道理的人，祝你们旅程成功。或者，像克林贡人说的，Qapla'！

93. You Can't Future-Proof Solutions

作者：Richard Monson-Haefel

Today’s Solution Is Tomorrow’s Problem

今天的方案是明天的问题

No one can predict the future. If you accept this as a universal truth, then the question becomes, how far ahead is the future? One decade? Two years? Twenty minutes? If you can’t predict the future, then you can’t predict anything beyond right now. This very moment and the ones that preceded it are all you are know until the next moment occurs. This is the reason we have car accidents; if you knew you were going to have an accident on Thursday, you would probably stay home.

没人能预测未来。如果你接受这是普世真理，问题变成：未来多远？十年？两年？二十分钟？如果你不能预测未来，你就不能预测现在以外的任何事。这个时刻和之前的时刻是你在下一时刻出现前所有知道的。这是我们有车祸的原因；如果你知道周四要出车祸，你可能会待家里。

Yet we see software architects try to design systems that will be, for lack of a better term, “future-proof” all the time. It’s simply not possible to futureproof an architecture. No matter what architectural decision you make now, that choice will become obsolete eventually. The cool programming language you used will eventually become the COBOL of tomorrow. Today’s distributed framework will become tomorrow’s DCOM. In short, today’s solution will always be tomorrow’s problem.

然而我们看到软件架构师一直试图设计「未来-proof」的系统（没更好的词）。架构不可能未来-proof。不管你现在做什么架构决定，那个选择最终会过时。你用的酷编程语言最终会成为明天的 COBOL。今天的分布式框架会成为明天的 DCOM。简言之，今天的方案永远是明天的问题。

If you accept this fact—that the choices you make today will most certainly be wrong in the future—then it relieves you of the burden of trying to futureproof your architectures. If any choice you make today will be a bad choice in the future, then don’t worry about what the future will hold—choose the best solution that meets your needs today.

如果你接受这个事实——你今天做的选择未来几乎肯定错——那它解除你试图未来-proof 架构的负担。如果你今天做的任何选择未来都会是坏选择，那别担心未来会怎样——选今天满足你需求的最佳方案。

One of the problems architects have today is analysis paralysis, and a big contribution to that problem is trying to guess the best technology for the future. Choosing a good technology for right now is hard enough; choosing one that will be relevant in the future is futile. Look at what your business needs now. Look at what the technology market offers now. Choose the best solution that meets your needs now, because anything else will not only be wrong choice tomorrow, but the wrong choice today.

今天架构师的一个问题是分析瘫痪，对这个问题大贡献是试图猜未来最佳技术。选现在好技术已经够难；选未来相关的是徒劳。看你业务现在需要什么。看技术市场现在提供什么。选现在满足你需求的最佳方案，因为其他任何选择不仅明天错、今天也错。

Richard Monson-Haefel Richard Monson-Haefel is an independent software developer who coauthored all five editions of Enterprise JavaBeans and both editions of Java Message Service (all O’Reilly). He’s a multitouch interface designer/developer and a leading expert on enterprise computing.

Richard Monson-Haefel Richard Monson-Haefel 是独立软件开发者，合著了 Enterprise JavaBeans 全部五版和 Java Message Service 两版（都是 O'Reilly）。他是多点触控界面设计师/开发者，企业计算领先专家。

94. The User Acceptance Problem

作者：Norman Carnovale

People aren’t always happy about new systems or major upgrades. This can pose a threat to the successful completion of a project.

人们不总是对新系统或大升级高兴。这可能威胁项目成功完成。

It’s not uncommon for people to disagree with the decision to implement a new system—especially at the beginning. This should be expected, and the reasons noted. However, initial reactions to a new system are less of a concern than a sustained negative reaction.

人们不同意实施新系统的决定并不少见——特别是一开始。这应该被预期，理由被记录。然而，对新系统的初始反应不如持续负面反应值得担心。

Your goal as an architect is to be aware of and measure the threat of acceptance problems and work toward mitigating those threats. To do this you have to be cognizant of them and consider the reasons for them. Some of the more common reasons are:

作为架构师你的目标是意识和衡量接受问题的威胁，并努力缓解这些威胁。要做到这点你必须认知它们、考虑原因。一些更常见原因是：

People may have concerns about the need for a new system (and subse- • quent retirement of an old system). This can also include fear of losing functionality or losing influence or power when roles change.

人们可能对需要新系统（以及随后旧系统退役）有顾虑。这还包括害怕失去功能、或角色变化时失去影响或权力。

People fear new (unproven) technology. •

人们怕新（未验证）技术。

People have cost/budget concerns. •

人们有成本/预算顾虑。

People simply do not like change. •

人们就是不喜欢变化。

Each of these reasons requires different possible solutions, some of which you can address and others you can’t. You have to recognize the difference and deal quickly with those that you can. Start early having discussions with your end users about the new system and its real and perceived benefits and disadvantages. The most effective long-term solution is to use the design of the system itself to address the concerns. Other effective solutions include training, scheduled system demonstrations (early in the project lifecycle), and sharing knowledge of what users will get with a new system.

每个原因需要不同可能方案，有些你能处理、有些不能。你必须认识区别，快速处理你能的。早点和最终用户讨论新系统及其真实和感知的优缺点。最有效的长期方案是用系统设计本身解决顾虑。其他有效方案包括培训、计划的系统演示（项目生命周期早期）、以及分享用户用新系统会得到什么的知识。

A “project champion” can help avoid user acceptance problems. Ideally this should be a person that represents the user group or stakeholders. This person sometimes has to be convinced himself. If there is none, then push for one from the very beginning. Once you’ve recruited a project champion, give him your assistance in every way you can.

「项目倡导者」能帮避免用户接受问题。理想情况下这应该是代表用户组或干系人的人。这个人有时需要被自己说服。如果没有，从最开始就推一个。一旦你招募了项目倡导者，尽你所能给他帮助。

95. The Importance of Consommé

作者：Eben Hewitt

A consommé is an extremely clarified broth,  usually made with beef or veal, served as a delicate soup. A well-made consommé is perfectly clear. It is considered challenging and time-consuming to make, because there is only one way to remove the fat and other solids that cloud the broth and gain the absolute clarity the dish requires: repeated, simple, fine-grained straining. This straining again and again, this hyperconscious refining of the mixture, creates an intensely rich flavor. It’s as if to taste a consommé is to taste the very essence of a thing. That is, in fact, the point of the dish.

清炖肉汤（consommé）是极清的 broth，通常用牛肉或小牛肉做，作为精致汤上。好做的 consommé 完全清澈。它被认为难做耗时，因为只有一种方法去除让 broth 浑浊的脂肪和其他固体、获得菜需要的绝对清澈：反复、简单、细粒度过滤。这种反复过滤、这种对混合物的超意识精炼，创造极浓的风味。就像尝 consommé 就是尝一个东西的精华。这其实就是菜的点。

In culinary schools in America, a simple test is administered to student chefs making consommé: the teacher drops a dime into your amber broth; if you can read the date on the dime resting at the bottom of the bowl, you pass. If you can’t, you fail.

美国烹饪学校里，对做 consommé 的学生厨师有个简单测试：老师把一枚十美分硬币扔进你的琥珀 broth；如果你能读出碗底那枚十美分上的日期，你过。不能，你挂。

Software architecture requires a continual refinement of thought, a repeated straining of ideas until we have determined the essence of each requirement in the system. We ask, like Hamlet holding Yorick’s skull, what is this thing? What are its properties? Its relations? We clarify our concepts, to make the relations within the architecture verifiably true, internally consistent.

软件架构要求持续精炼思想、反复过滤想法，直到我们确定系统里每个需求的精华。我们像 Hamlet 拿着 Yorick 的头骨那样问：这是什么？它的属性？它的关系？我们澄清概念，让架构内的关系可验证为真、内部一致。

Many missed requirements and bugs in software can be traced to ambiguous, general language. Ask customers, developers, analysts, and users the same questions repeatedly, until they are drowsy with boredom. Now disguise your question to pose it in a different way, like an attorney looking for a snag in the alibi, to tease out anything new, any differences or contradictions. Strain and strain again.

软件里很多漏掉的需求和 bug 可追溯到模糊、一般的语言。反复问客户、开发、分析师和用户同样问题，直到他们烦得打瞌睡。现在把你的问题伪装成另一种方式问，像律师找不在场证明的破绽，挑出任何新东西、任何差异或矛盾。滤了再滤。

Focus on what can be removed from the concepts presented in the architecture, the nouns that compose them, to determine their essence. Bring surgical precision to the language you find in your requirements, rejecting ambiguity, generality, unwarranted assumptions, or extraneous verbiage. This serves to make your concepts richer, more robust. Reduce and reduce again.

聚焦从架构呈现的概念、组成它们的名词里能移除什么，来确定它们的精华。给你在需求里找到的语言带来外科手术般的精确，拒绝模糊、一般性、无根据假设、或多余废话。这让你的概念更丰富、更健壮。减了再减。

Test statements by asking “Would you make the same statement if I appended ‘always and forever and in every circumstance’ to it?” People resist committing to absolutes like this, and must refine their words. Force representations of concepts through a linguistic sieve to clarify them. Do this again, until you are left with only the exhaustive list of simple and verifiably true statements that describe the essential nature of the system.

用「如果我给它加上'永远在任何情况下都'你会做同样陈述吗？」测试陈述。人们抗拒承诺这种绝对，必须精炼他们的话。强迫概念表示通过语言筛子来澄清。再做，直到你只剩描述系统本质的简单、可验证为真的陈述穷举列表。

You’ll know when the architecture is finished: when you can look through it and read the date on a dime.

你会知道架构什么时候完成：当你能看穿它、读出十美分上的日期。

96. For the End User, the Interface Is the System

作者：Vinayak Hegde

There are too many good products hidden behind bad user-interfaces. The end user will access the system through its user interface. If the quality of the user’s experience while interacting with your product suffers, then his impression of your product will suffer, no matter how technologically advanced and path-breaking your product might be.

太多好产品藏在差用户界面后面。最终用户通过用户界面访问系统。如果用户和你产品交互时体验质量受损，他对你产品的印象就会受损，不管你产品技术多先进、多开路。

The user interface is an important component of architecture and an oftenneglected one. The architect should enlist the services of specialists such as user experience designers and usability experts. The user interaction experts, along with the architect, can drive the interface design as well as its coupling with the internal mechanisms. Involving user interface experts at an early stage and throughout the product development phases ensures that the final product is polished, and that the integration of the user interface with the product is seamless. The architect should also look at doing user interaction testing while the product is still in beta with actual end users, and incorporate their feedback into the final product.

用户界面是架构的重要组成部分，经常被忽略。架构师应该招募用户体验设计师和可用性专家这样的专家服务。用户交互专家和架构师一起，能驱动界面设计及其与内部机制的耦合。早期和整个产品开发阶段让用户界面专家参与，确保最终产品打磨、用户界面和产品集成无缝。架构师还应该在产品 beta 时和实际最终用户做用户交互测试，把他们的反馈融入最终产品。

Often the usage of a product changes over time as technology changes and features are added. The architect should ensure that user interface changes with the architecture reflect the expectations of the users.

通常产品用法随技术变化和加功能随时间改变。架构师应该确保随架构变化的用户界面反映用户期望。

User interactions should be one of the goals of the complete product architecture. In fact, user interaction should be an integral part of the decisionmaking process for architecture tradeoffs and internal product documentation as much as robustness and performance. Changes in user interaction design should be captured over time, just like code. This is especially true in products where the user interface is written in a different programming language than the rest of the product.

用户交互应该是完整产品架构的目标之一。实际上，用户交互应该和健壮性、性能一样，成为架构权衡和内部产品文档决策过程的组成部分。用户交互设计的变化应该随时间被捕捉，像代码一样。用户界面用和产品其他部分不同编程语言写的产品尤其如此。

It is the architect’s responsibility to make the most common interactions not only easy but also rewarding for the end user. Better user interfaces lead to happier customers , which helps improve customer productivity. If your product helps people become more productive, then it will contribute to the business’s bottom-line.

架构师的责任是让最常见交互不仅容易，而且对最终用户有回报。更好的用户界面带来更快乐的客户，帮提升客户生产力。如果你的产品帮人更高产，它会贡献业务底线。

Vinayak Hegde Vinayak Hegde is a geek interested in computers, photography, and entrepreneurship. He is currently working as an architect with Akamai Technologies.

Vinayak Hegde Vinayak Hegde 是对计算机、摄影和创业感兴趣的极客。他目前在 Akamai Technologies 做架构师。

97. Great Software Is Not Built, It Is Grown

作者：Bill de hÓra

As an architect, you are tasked with providing the initial structure and arrangement of software systems that will grow and change over time, will have to be reworked, and will have to talk to other systems—and almost always in ways you and your stakeholders did not foresee. Even though we are called architects , and we borrow many metaphors from building and engineering, great software is not built, it is grown.

作为架构师，你的任务是提供软件系统的初始结构和安排——这些系统会随时间生长变化、需要返工、必须和其他系统对话——而且几乎总是以你和干系人没预见的方式。虽然我们被叫架构师、从建筑和工程借很多隐喻，伟大软件不是被建出来的，是被长出来的。

The single biggest predictor of software failure is size; on reflection there’s almost no benefit to be had from starting with a large system design. Yet at some point we will all be tempted to do exactly that. As well as being prone to incidental complexity and inertia, designing large systems upfront means larger projects, which are more likely to fail, more likely to be untestable, more likely to be fragile, more likely to have unneeded and unused parts, more likely to be expensive, and more likely to have a negative political dimension.

软件失败最大单一预测因子是规模；反思一下，从大系统设计开始几乎没好处。然而某个时候我们都会被诱惑那么做。除了容易有附带复杂度和惯性，前期设计大系统意味着更大项目——更可能失败、更可能不可测、更可能脆弱、更可能有不需要和没用的部分、更可能贵、更可能有负面政治维度。

Therefore resist trying to design a large complete system to “meet or exceed” the known requirements and desired properties, no matter how tempting that might be. Have a grand vision, but not a grand design. Let you and your system learn to adapt as the situation and requirements inevitably change.

因此，抵制设计一个大完整系统来「满足或超过」已知需求和期望属性的冲动，不管那多诱人。有宏大愿景，但不要宏大设计。让你和你的系统学会在情况和需求不可避免变化时适应。

How to do this? The best way to ensure that a software system can evolve and adapt is to evolve and adapt it from the very outset. Inducing a system to evolve means starting with a small running system, a working subset of the intended architecture—the simplest thing that could possibly work. This nascent system will have many desirable properties and can teach us much

怎么做？确保软件系统能演化适应的最好方法是从一开始就演化适应它。诱导系统演化意味着从一个小运行系统开始、一个预期架构的工作子集——最简单可能工作的东西。这个新生系统会有很多理想属性，

about the architecture that a large system, or worse, a collection of architectural documents, never can. You are more likely to have been involved in its implementation. Its lack of surface area will be easier to test and therefore less prone to coupling. It will require a smaller team, which will reduce the cost of coordinating the project. Its properties will be easier to observe. It will be easier to deploy. It will teach you and your team at the earliest possible moment what does and does not work. It will tell you where the system will not evolve easily, where it is likely to crystallize, where it is fragile. Where it might break. Perhaps most important, it will be comprehensible and tangible to its stakeholders from the beginning, allowing them to grow into the overall design as well.

能教我们大系统——或更糟，一堆架构文档——永远不能教的关于架构的东西。你更可能参与了它的实现。它的小表面积更容易测、因此更不易耦合。它需要更小团队，降低协调项目成本。它的属性更容易观察。它更容易部署。它会在最早可能时刻教你和团队什么工作什么不工作。它会告诉你系统在哪不容易演化、在哪可能结晶、在哪脆弱。哪可能断。也许最重要的是，它从一开始就对干系人可理解和可触摸，让他们也能长入整体设计。

Design the smallest system you can, help deliver it, and let it evolve toward the grand vision. Although this might feel like giving up control, or even shirking your responsibilities, ultimately your stakeholders will thank you for it. Do not confuse an evolutionary approach with throwing requirements out, the dreaded phasing, or building one to throw away.

设计你能设计的最小系统，帮交付它，让它朝宏大愿景演化。虽然这可能感觉像放弃控制、甚至逃避责任，最终你的干系人会感谢你。不要把演化方法和扔需求、可怕的分期、或建一个扔掉的混为一谈。
